issues.title: Exact order-one substitution outside the Caputo definition

failure_location.quote:
In particular, $\alpha\left(t\right)\equiv1$
and $\beta\left(t\right)\equiv1$ reduce the system to the 
standard incompressible MHD equations \cite{He2018}.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that setting alpha(t)=beta(t)=1 exactly in the displayed fractional system reduces it to classical MHD. The old paper actually defines its Caputo operator only for strict orders between zero and one, so it supplies no operator at the asserted endpoint; only the limiting interpretation as the orders approach one is supported. The material difference is exact substitution into an undefined endpoint versus a formal classical-order limit.
issues.overall_effect: The exact endpoint statement is not literally licensed by the model definition. This does not affect the analysis for orders strictly below one or the separately implemented integer-order reference computation.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Treat the classical case as an explicitly defined endpoint extension: retain the integral formula for 0<ν(t)<1, separately define the order-one operator by {}^C D_t^1 f=∂_t f, and state that the exact α=β=1 reduction uses this convention. The strict-order analysis can remain unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The old source has a genuine missing endpoint definition rather than a uniquely forced transcriptional error. Adding the standard order-one convention is a short, routine local repair that preserves the exact classical-reduction claim and does not affect any analysis, rate, computation, or dependent result.

new_version_repair_locator.quote:
When $\nu\left(t\right)\to 1$, this prefactor tends to 1, and the fractional derivative formally approaches the classical first-order derivative.
Thus, in the limiting case $\alpha\left(t\right),\beta\left(t\right)\to 1$, the system (\ref{eq:given_u1})--(\ref{eq:eq:eq:given_B2}) reduces to the standard

issues.title: Noncoercive corrected-energy estimate presented as stability
issues.failure_explanation: The theorem's Stability label and associated prose can suggest control of the solution norm, while its displayed conclusion bounds a corrected memory functional. That functional subtracts a nonnegative history term from the energy, and the source supplies no coercive lower bound connecting it to the physical solution norm. The established defect is misleading presentation of the corrected-functional estimate; the theorem does not explicitly display a uniform solution-norm bound.
issues.overall_effect: The corrected-functional estimate alone does not establish discrete norm stability. This allegation establishes neither falsity of the displayed inequality nor instability of the scheme. No dependent formal conclusion needs alteration for this formulation repair; the convergence theorem uses a separate argument.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Rename the result Corrected-memory estimate and align the abstract, introduction, and surrounding stability language with its actual conclusion. Explicitly state that this estimate alone does not establish a uniform solution-norm bound. Preserve the displayed inequality and its assumptions; an additional common-order norm-stability theorem is not required to repair this presentation issue.
issues.why_classification: On the contextual reading, the precise mathematical conclusion is already the corrected-functional inequality. A local clarification of its label and description preserves that conclusion and supports minor. This assessment does not apply to a stronger allegation that an explicitly promised general solution-norm stability theorem must be replaced or restricted.

issues.title: Wrong sign in the magnetic divergence-cleaning projection

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In the periodic test cases, ({\ref{eq:elliptic}) is solved with periodic boundary conditions

issues.failure_explanation: The executable cleaning step solves the old positive-sign elliptic equation and then subtracts grad phi from the magnetic field. Under periodic integration by parts, these two instructions add the original weak divergence instead of canceling it. With the revised negative right-hand side, (div B_h^n,psi_h)=(div tilde B_h^n,psi_h)+(grad phi_h^n,grad psi_h)=0.
issues.overall_effect: If followed literally in the periodic computations, the stated postprocessing step doubles rather than removes the weak magnetic divergence, so its cleaning contract and prose claims of post-cleaning reduction do not follow. The formal stability and convergence results analyze Problem prob:fully without this postprocessing and are not dependent formal results.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the missing minus sign in the elliptic problem, so that (∇φ_h^n,∇ψ_h)=−(∇·B̃_h^n,ψ_h), while retaining B_h^n=B̃_h^n−∇φ_h^n. Periodic integration by parts then gives (∇·B_h^n,ψ_h)=0.
issues.why_classification: With the subtraction update fixed, the stated divergence-cleaning purpose and the periodic weak identity uniquely force the negative right-hand side. This is a single transcriptional sign correction requiring no new construction, proof architecture, weakened guarantee, or change to the independent stability and convergence results.
